name: Pentose Phosphate Pathway (Oxidative and Non-Oxidative Branches)
description: The pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) provides NADPH for biosynthetic reactions and pentose sugars for nucleotide synthesis. It consists of two phases: the oxidative phase generating NADPH and the non-oxidative phase recycling pentose phosphates into glycolytic intermediates. The pathway branches based on cellular needs for NADPH versus ribose-5-phosphate.
scientificAccuracy: This representation is based on well-characterized enzymatic steps in E. coli glucose metabolism, validated by decades of biochemical studies. The pathway's two-phase structure (oxidative and non-oxidative) reflects the cell's ability to balance NADPH production with pentose sugar synthesis.

mermaid:
graph TD
    Start([Glucose-6-Phosphate Available]) --> G6PD[G6PDH: Glucose-6-P + NADP+]
    G6PD --> P6GL[6-Phosphogluconolactone + NADPH]
    P6GL --> PGL[6-Phosphogluconolactonase]
    PGL --> P6G[6-Phosphogluconate]
    P6G --> PGDH[6-PGDH: 6-Phosphogluconate + NADP+]
    PGDH --> Ru5P[Ribulose-5-P + NADPH + CO2]
    
    Ru5P --> BranchPoint{{Cellular Need?}}
    BranchPoint -->|Need NADPH| RecycleOx[Oxidative Phase Complete]
    BranchPoint -->|Need Ribose-5-P| IsomeraseRoute[Phosphopentose Isomerase]
    
    IsomeraseRoute --> R5P[Ribose-5-P]
    R5P --> NucleotidePath{{Use Ribose?}}
    NucleotidePath -->|Yes| NucleoSynth[Nucleotide Biosynthesis]
    NucleotidePath -->|No| NonOxPhase[Enter Non-Oxidative Phase]
    
    Ru5P --> Epimerase[Phosphopentose Epimerase]
    Epimerase --> X5P[Xylulose-5-P]
    
    NonOxPhase --> TransketolaseCheck[Transketolase Available?]
    TransketolaseCheck -->|Yes| TK1[Transketolase Reaction 1]
    R5P --> TK1
    X5P --> TK1
    TK1 --> S7P[Sedoheptulose-7-P]
    TK1 --> G3P1[Glyceraldehyde-3-P]
    
    S7P --> TAL[Transaldolase]
    G3P1 --> TAL
    TAL --> F6P1[Fructose-6-P]
    TAL --> E4P[Erythrose-4-P]
    
    E4P --> TK2[Transketolase Reaction 2]
    X5P --> TK2
    TK2 --> F6P2[Fructose-6-P]
    TK2 --> G3P2[Glyceraldehyde-3-P]
    
    F6P1 --> GlycRoute{{Return to Glycolysis?}}
    F6P2 --> GlycRoute
    GlycRoute -->|Yes| Glycolysis[Glycolysis Pathway]
    GlycRoute -->|No| RecycleG6P[Convert back to G6P]
    
    G3P2 --> TriosePool[Triose Phosphate Pool]
    TriosePool --> GlycoEntry{{Enter Glycolysis?}}
    GlycoEntry -->|Yes| LowerGlyc[Lower Glycolysis]
    GlycoEntry -->|No| Gluconeo[Gluconeogenesis]
    
    RecycleOx --> NADPH1[NADPH for Biosynthesis]
    NADPH1 --> FattyAcid{{Fatty Acid Synthesis?}}
    FattyAcid -->|Yes| FABiosyn[Membrane Lipid Biosynthesis]
    FattyAcid -->|No| OtherBiosyn[Other Biosynthetic Pathways]
    
    NADPH1 --> Antioxidant{{Oxidative Stress?}}
    Antioxidant -->|Yes| GlutathioneRed[Glutathione Reduction]
    Antioxidant -->|No| StoredNADPH[NADPH Pool Available]
    
    NucleoSynth --> PurineCheck{{Purine OR Pyrimidine?}}
    PurineCheck -->|Purine| PurinePath[Purine Nucleotide Synthesis]
    PurineCheck -->|Pyrimidine| PyrimPath[Pyrimidine Nucleotide Synthesis]
    
    RecycleG6P --> ReenterPPP{{Re-enter PPP?}}
    ReenterPPP -->|Yes| G6PD
    ReenterPPP -->|No| Storage[Glucose-6-P Storage]
    
    Glycolysis --> ATP[ATP Production]
    LowerGlyc --> Pyruvate[Pyruvate]
    Pyruvate --> EndProduct([Central Metabolism])
    
    PurinePath --> DNA_RNA1[DNA/RNA Synthesis]
    PyrimPath --> DNA_RNA2[DNA/RNA Synthesis]
    FABiosyn --> Membranes([Cell Membrane Components])
    GlutathioneRed --> CellProtect([Cellular Protection])
    OtherBiosyn --> Metabolites([Biosynthetic Intermediates])
    ATP --> Energy([Cellular Energy])
